subject: Offer letter — proration of signing bonus, probation language, and first payroll window
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Draft offer for Alex Jordan — guidance on bonus proration & probation wording

Hi all,

Attaching a first-pass offer for Alex Jordan (Senior Backend Engineer, remote - US). Key comp points are below:
- Base: $185,000 (E3 band)
- Signing bonus: $25,000 (we typically discuss paying on first payroll or split)
- Start target: Dec 7, 2026 (candidate preference)

A few open questions where I need input before I send the formal offer:
1) Signing bonus proration: Should we pay full bonus on first payroll regardless of start date, or pro-rate if start is mid-pay-cycle? Current internal habit is to pro-rate if start after day 10 of the month but I want alignment.
2) Probation language: Hiring manager asked for a 90-day probation vs default 180-day in some teams. Do we want to hold back part of the signing bonus until probation completion?
3) Immigration/background: Candidate is on STEM OPT — do we need explicit immigration assistance language or just the standard contingent-on-clearance clause?
4) Payroll window: Candidate is asking about when bonus would hit (first payroll vs next month). Our payroll runs the 15th and last-day pay with a
two-business-day cutoff. Is proration policy documented anywhere I can link?

Draft attached: AJ-offer-draft-20261122.docx (stubs only).

Plan: if we agree, I'll incorporate Mark's suggested clause and loop in payroll for payment timing.

Thanks — quick replies welcome, planning to send to candidate by EOD Tue if we have language.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Talent Partner | Redwood Inference
--
Attachment: AJ-offer-draft-20261122.docx (offer letter draft, DOCX)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 11:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft offer for Alex Jordan — guidance on bonus proration & probation wording

Jasmine — quick notes from comp side:
- Band: E3 confirmed for Sr Backend Eng, base $185k OK.
- Signing bonus: we usually pro-rate signing bonuses when start date is after the 10th of the month to avoid partial-month overpayments. Suggest pro-rating by calendar days in the first payroll period.
- Probation: 90 days is fine for this role. My only ask is that we tie the second tranche of the signing bonus to completion of 90 days to encourage retention. Suggested split: 50% on first payroll, 50% after 90 days.
- If candidate pushes for full upfront, we can approve one-off but would need a note to finance and exec approval for the exception (I can sign off if only base+bonus totals under $220k net new comp).

If that works I can flag as approved and you can push to legal for language.

— Vivek
VP, Engineering (Hiring Manager)

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft offer for Alex Jordan — guidance on bonus proration & probation wording

Thanks — drafting suggested language and attaching a short redline. High level:
- Probation period: 90 days (we can accept).
- Signing bonus payment schedule (recommended):
  "Signing Bonus Payment Schedule: Employee will receive 50% of the signing bonus on the first payroll after the Start Date, subject to normal payroll withholding. The remaining 50% will be payable upon successful completion of the 90-day probationary period, provided the Employee is actively employed on the payment date. Redwood reserves the right to claw back bonus amounts if employment terminates for cause before the second payment."
- Contingencies: Add explicit language that the offer is contingent on satisfactory background check and verification of work authorization; for OPT candidates include the standard "company may provide immigration support at its discretion" sentence.
- Payroll timing: recommend we avoid promising specific calendar dates in the offer; instead say "payment will be made in Redwood's next regularly scheduled payroll after the applicable payment event." That reduces risk.

Attachment: probation_clause_suggestion_20261123.pdf (PDF with redline snippets).

If comp is ok with 50/50 split, I'll incorporate the clause and circulate final. If hiring wants full upfront payment, we need a one-off approval and an exec note (Vivek said he can approve up to the threshold).

-Markus
General Counsel | Redwood Inference
--
Attachment: probation_clause_suggestion_20261123.pdf (redline, PDF)

From: Alex Jordan <alex.jordan@outlook.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft offer for Alex Jordan — guidance on bonus proration & probation wording

Hi Jasmine — thanks for the update and for pulling this together. Really excited about the role and the team. A couple of quick asks before you finalize:

1) Start date: I can do Dec 7, 2026 as proposed. Is there any flexibility to move earlier to Dec 1 if paperwork completes? I have a short notice period to my current contractor client but could potentially finish earlier.

2) Signing bonus timing: I understand the company practice. Would Redwood consider paying the full $25,000 on the first payroll? I need the funds for a lease deposit and bank transfer deadlines are tight. If not possible, would the 50/50 split with the first tranche being on the first payroll work for my timing?

3) OPT status: I am on STEM OPT (EAD valid until 04/30/2027). I'll provide the documents. I'm evaluating sponsor options but appreciate that Redwood will provide immigration support at discretion.

4) Payroll/proration: if we go with proration for a mid-month start, could you include a short sentence in the offer that explains how proration will be calculated (e.g., prorated by days in the first payroll period)? That will help me plan cashflow.

Attached is my signed candidate info sheet (stub). Happy to hop on a 15-min call if it's easier.

Best,
Alex Jordan
alex.jordan@outlook.com
--
Attachment: AJ-candidate-info-20261125.pdf (candidate info, PDF)
